:::{#thm-trace-cyclic}
#### The trace of a product does not depend on the order

For an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$ and an $n \times m$ matrix $\matr{B}$:

$$
\operatorname{tr}\paren{\underbrace{\matr{A}\matr{B}}_{m \times m}}
= \operatorname{tr}\paren{\underbrace{\matr{B}\matr{A}}_{n \times n}}
$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\operatorname{tr}(\matr{A}\matr{B})
&= \sum_{i=1}^{m} (\matr{A}\matr{B})_{ii}
&& \text{(definition of the trace)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^{m} \sum_{s=1}^{n} a_{is}\, b_{si}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \sum_{s=1}^{n} \sum_{i=1}^{m} a_{is}\, b_{si}
&& \text{(swap the order of two finite sums)}
\\
&= \sum_{s=1}^{n} \sum_{i=1}^{m} b_{si}\, a_{is}
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)}
\\
&= \sum_{s=1}^{n} (\matr{B}\matr{A})_{ss}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \operatorname{tr}(\matr{B}\matr{A})
&& \text{(definition of the trace)}
\ea
$$

:::

::: notes
$\matr{A}\matr{B}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{A}$ need not have the same size,
so @thm-trace-cyclic can equate the traces of an $m \times m$ matrix
and an $n \times n$ matrix.
Applying it to $\matr{A}$ and the product $\matr{B}\matr{C}$
moves the last factor of a triple product to the front:
$\operatorname{tr}(\matr{A}\matr{B}\matr{C}) = \operatorname{tr}(\matr{C}\matr{A}\matr{B})$
[@banerjee2014linear, Chapter 1, Theorem 1.5 and eq. 1.17, p. 19].
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-trace-cyclic}
#### Traces of the two products of a $2 \times 3$ and a $3 \times 2$ matrix

Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

Then

$$
\matr{A}\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
\qquad
\matr{B}\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{tr}(\matr{A}\matr{B}) = 5 + 4 = 9
\qquad
\operatorname{tr}(\matr{B}\matr{A}) = 1 + 5 + 3 = 9
$$

The products have different sizes, but their traces agree.

:::
